  • Enterprise architecture documentation lags reality

The EA ends up trapped between what should be—and what actually is.

What this means for the EA role

1) From planner to enabler

The EA can no longer act primarily as a central planner. Instead, they must become an enabler and coach—someone who empowers decentralized teams to make architecturally sound decisions without having to personally make every decision.

“Architecture is not about control; it's about enabling good decisions at scale.”

2) From static models to a living landscape

Instead of complex, one-off architecture models, what’s needed are lightweight artifacts that are maintained continuously: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), living wikis, automatically generated landscape maps. The model has to be able to breathe.

3) From framework dogmatism to pragmatism

TOGAF phases and Zachman cells have their value—but in a world of continuous transformation, EA methods must be applied situationally and pragmatically. No framework fits every situation unchanged.

4) From silo guardian to bridge builder

The EA must actively build bridges: between IT and business, between strategic planning and operational execution, between innovation and governance. Stay in your silo—and you lose relevance.

What the EA needs to avoid freezing up

Technical competence still matters

Even as the EA becomes more strategic, they must understand what’s happening technically—AI, cloud-native architectures, API ecosystems, data platforms. Credibility comes from competence, not from titles.

Communication is a core skill

The best architecture plan is useless if no one understands it. EAs must learn to explain complex things simply—at board level and in engineering teams alike.

Resilience and ambiguity tolerance

Transformation means uncertainty. No complete picture, no final answers—just the ability to remain effective anyway and move forward iteratively.

Networking and visibility

Enterprise architecture doesn’t happen in a back room. The EA must be visible, present, and connected—across projects, committees, and communities of practice. If you’re not heard, you’ll be bypassed.

The “off script” role: the EA as Data Migration Lead

No topic in S/4HANA projects is underestimated as consistently as data migration. It’s not a technical side quest—it’s the foundation the entire new world stands on. And that’s exactly why it lands with the EA: because it’s critical, messy, and “kind of technical.” The implicit assumption being, of course, that the EA can simply absorb a full-scale data migration on top of their existing responsibilities—no additional headcount, no external support, no problem. Spoiler: no. For a while, he'll have to unlearn what has become second nature.

By doing so, the EA deliberately steps out of the classic role. They’re no longer the architect at the drawing board, but the Data Migration Lead—archaeologist, diplomat, and crisis manager all in one. This role shift isn’t a failure. It’s a strategic investment in a skill set that most EAs only ever talk about.

What challenges the EA here

The migration topics are multifaceted—and each is its own discipline:

  • Business Partner: customers from Fxxxxx, Ixxxxx, and Nxxxxxxx must be consolidated into a central SAP Business Partner—without duplicates, with clear role logic (customer, supplier, prospect) and consistent master data.
  • Article & material master: color codes, product groups, season flags, and size logic from the source systems must be mapped to a unified S/4HANA data model. Every wrong mapping hits inventory, logistics, and reporting immediately.
  • Open orders: purchase orders and sales orders that span the go-live cutover date must be migrated completely and correctly—no order can be lost.
  • Inventory: the hardest exercise. Physical stock and migrated values must match exactly. Phantom stock and unexplained variances always show up precisely when you need them least. And the quality bar is brutal: inventory values worth several million euros are transferred into the new system. Any deviation hits the balance sheet—and inevitably triggers the auditor. They’ll ask politely—once. After that, the tone tends to change.

What the EA gains from it

This role shift isn’t a detour—it’s an investment in a competence profile no textbook can teach:

  • Deep business understanding: if you know how data really flows, you understand the company at a level no org chart or process model can capture.
  • Stakeholder trust: the EA who has worked in the engine room is taken seriously by business and leadership alike—they’ve proven they can deliver.
  • Architectural credibility: post-migration decisions on data governance, master data management, and system integration are no longer theory—they’re lived experience.
  • Career relevance: data-migration expertise is scarce and in demand. Anyone who has led an S/4HANA migration becomes a highly relevant leader for future transformations—internally and externally.
  • A foundation for real refactoring: after go-live, the EA knows exactly where the technical debt is, which compromises were made, and where cleanup must start. That makes them the best architect for the next phase.

LeanIX: the quiet hero nobody misses—until it’s gone

If you’ve lived through an S/4HANA transformation, you know this moment: someone asks, “Which systems are actually connected to Nxxxxxxx?” or “Who is the business owner of the integration interface to Fxxxxx?” And suddenly everyone looks around.

That’s when LeanIX’s relevance goes through the roof.

LeanIX is the EA’s central tool for application portfolio management and documenting the IT landscape. In calm times, many see it as a nice-to-have—a maintenance tool you “should update at some point.” Keeping LeanIX current when everything is quiet? “We’ll do it after the project.” The project lasts five years. Welcome to the vicious cycle. In a transformation, it turns into critical infrastructure.

Why LeanIX becomes non-negotiable in transformation

  • Make dependencies visible: which applications depend on the legacy systems being decommissioned? Which interfaces must be migrated—and which can be shut down? Without maintained LeanIX, these are assumptions, not facts.
  • Steer the coexistence phase: while old and new systems run in parallel, LeanIX can be the only source that keeps an overview of the landscape state—if it’s kept up to date.
  • Justify migration decisions: which application gets replaced, which stays? Which is technically outdated, which still has strategic relevance? LeanIX provides the data basis for those decisions.
  • Communicate with stakeholders: a maintained LeanIX portfolio replaces endless PowerPoint decks. It makes transformation progress visible—for management and project teams alike.

The bitter paradox

LeanIX is often valued only when the data is missing or out of date: when, during the cutover crunch, nobody can say which system is still writing data into Nxxxxxxx. When the interface documentation dates back to 2016—and reality has long since moved on.

The EA is often the only person who knows why a decision was made years ago—and is politely blamed for it today. That knowledge lives in no ticket, no Confluence page, and no LeanIX record. It sits in their head. If you don’t trust the EA, you’re not really trusting the long-term sustainability of your own IT landscape.

The EA who maintained LeanIX consistently before the transformation is the calmest person in the room in that moment. The EA who didn’t is the one who spends the next weeks reconstructing the landscape through interviews and manual analysis—under time pressure.

Good LeanIX maintenance isn’t bureaucracy. It’s the insurance you never miss—until you need it.

Transformation is also a chance to establish LeanIX permanently: not as “the EA team’s job”, but as a living tool owned by the entire IT organization.

Conclusion: more than an architect

Anyone who lives through this kind of transformation doesn’t come back the same. The EA has worked in the engine room as a Data Migration Lead, defended LeanIX under pressure, mediated across business units, and filled roles that were never in their job description. They outgrew themselves—usually when they had no other choice.

The most valuable skills they take away don’t initially sound like enterprise architecture: data quality, stakeholder diplomacy, operational crisis-readiness, systems thinking under pressure. But that’s exactly what separates a great EA from a good one.

These capabilities aren’t side activities—they’re the multiplier for everything the EA wants to deliver strategically. If you don’t know how data really flows, you design architectures in a vacuum. If you don’t have credibility in day-to-day operations, you won’t be heard strategically.

Your target architecture is beautiful. But reality will still ruin it—slowly, over time and within budget. And the project even has the board’s full support for these unsustainable decisions.

And LeanIX? Next time, they’ll update it first—not because someone demands it, but because they know what happens when nobody does.

The transformation wasn’t a detour. It was the shortest path to becoming a better architect.

In the end, nobody got exactly what they imagined. Everyone still emerged stronger—but everyone walks out with something rare: the shared credibility of having steered the company through the messy part — together, and often well outside their job descriptions.

That's transformation!

entry.title: Good to Know Series #6 Migrating Customer Business Partners Using the Fiori App "Migrate Your Data"
entry.content:
Good to Know Series # 6
Migrating Customer Business Partners Using the Fiori App "Migrate Your Data" in SAP S/4HANA 2025
Introduction
One of the most important activities in any SAP implementation or S/4HANA migration project is migrating master data.
Without Customer Business Partners, users cannot create Sales Orders, Deliveries, or Billing Documents. Therefore, ensuring that customer master data is migrated correctly is one of the first priorities during project implementation.
SAP provides a standard Fiori application called Migrate Your Data, which offers a guided, step-by-step process to migrate master data into SAP S/4HANA.
In this blog, I'll walk you through the complete process of migrating Customer Business Partners using the Migrate Your Data Fiori app in SAP S/4HANA 2025.
Along the way, I'll also share a few practical tips that have helped me during implementation projects.
________________________________________
Step 1
Access the Fiori App
Log in to the SAP Fiori Launchpad.
Search for and open the Migrate Your Data app.

________________________________________
Step 2
Create a New Migration Project
Click Create to create a new migration project.
Choose the migration approach.
For this example, we'll use:
Migrate Data Using Staging Tables

Enter:
• Project Name
• Database Connection as “Local SAP S/4HANA Database Schema”.
Click Step 2.

________________________________________
Select the Development Package
Choose the required Development Package.
Click Step 3.

 

____________________________________
Select the Migration Object
Search for and select the migration object:
Customer
You can select one or multiple migration objects depending on your business requirement.
The selected objects will appear on the right-hand side.
Click Review.

________________________________________
A popup window appears asking whether predecessor objects should also be included.
If they are not required, simply click Do Not Add.

Now click Create Project.

The migration project is now created successfully. Open the project to continue.

________________________________________

Step 3
In this Step the system will take considerable time.

You can click on Monitoring button, to view the status.

Once the Migration object is ready, Click on “Mapping Tasks”.

On Clicking the Mapping tasks

Select the Items and Click on Confirm after entering the values, continue the same for other item.

Download the Migration Template
Inside the migration project, click Download Template.

SAP downloads an XML template that contains all the required fields for Customer migration.

Download and save the XML file on your desktop. Open the XML file using Microsoft Excel.
You'll notice that the template contains multiple worksheets for different types of customer information.
For example:
• General Data

• BP Roles

• Company Code Data

• Sales Area Data

Not every worksheet is mandatory.
Maintain only the sheets that are relevant to your migration scenario.

________________________________________
Fill the Migration Template
Enter the required customer information such as:
• Customer Number
• Customer Name
• Address
• Country
• Language
• Company Code
• Reconciliation Account
• Payment Terms
• Sales Organization
• Distribution Channel
• Division
Save the XML file after entering the data.
________________________________________
Project Tip
For your very first migration, I strongly recommend maintaining only one customer record.
This makes it much easier to identify validation errors and understand the migration process before uploading hundreds or thousands of customers.
Once everything works successfully, you can proceed with larger data volumes.
________________________________________
Step 4
Upload the Prepared File
Return to the migration project.
Upload the completed XML template.
SAP validates the file structure automatically.

After uploading the file, go back to the Migration Project and click Monitoring.

Click Prepare to start preparing the staging tables.

Wait until the status changes successfully.

On this activity system may take more time in Preparing the staging tables.

________________________________________
Step 5
Complete Mapping Tasks
Once preparation is completed, open Mapping Tasks.

SAP automatically maps most of the values.
Review the mappings carefully.
You can either:
• Confirm each mapping individually
or
• Select all mappings and click Confirm.

Once all mapping tasks are confirmed, return to the Monitoring screen.
________________________________________
Step 6
Simulate the Migration
Now click Simulate.

SAP checks all uploaded data before actually creating Business Partners.
This is one of the most important steps.
Never skip Simulation.

It helps identify missing mandatory fields, invalid configuration values, or incorrect mappings before any data is created in the system.
________________________________________
Common Validation Errors
During Simulation, you may encounter errors like:
• Company Code does not exist
• Sales Organization is invalid
• Reconciliation Account missing
• Payment Terms invalid
• Mandatory field missing
• Duplicate Customer Number
• Invalid Country Code
• Missing Business Partner Role
Resolve all validation errors before proceeding.
________________________________________
Step 7
Execute the Migration
Once the Simulation completes successfully without errors, click Migrate Data.

You are going to migrate data. The migration cannot be undone. Are you sure you want to continue?

SAP starts creating the Customer Business Partners.
Monitor the migration progress from the Monitoring screen.


After successful completion, the status changes to Completed.

Click on Migration results.

________________________________________
Step 8

Verify the Migrated Data
Now verify the migrated Business Partners.
Open:
• BP
• Display Business Partner
You can also verify the data using the relevant database tables if required.
Check that the following information has been migrated correctly:
• General Data
• Company Code Data
• Sales Area Data
• Payment Terms
• Reconciliation Account
• Tax Classification
• Address
• Partner Functions

________________________________________
Step 9
Complete the Migration Project
Once everything has been verified successfully, return to the Migrate Your Data app and mark the migration project as Completed.
You can now inform the business users that the customer migration has been completed successfully.
________________________________________
Things to Remember
Even though the migration completes successfully, always verify the following before handing over the system to the business.
✔ Business Partner created successfully
✔ Customer Roles (FLCU00 and FLCU01)
✔ Company Code Data
✔ Sales Area Data
✔ Payment Terms
✔ Reconciliation Account
✔ Partner Functions
✔ Tax Classification
✔ Address Details
✔ Search Terms
A few minutes spent verifying the data can save hours of correction later.
________________________________________
Conclusion
Migrating Customer Business Partners is one of the most important activities during an SAP S/4HANA implementation or migration project.
The Migrate Your Data Fiori app provides a simple and guided approach that helps consultants migrate master data efficiently while reducing manual effort.
One recommendation from my project experience is to always start with a single customer record. Once the migration is successful and validated, proceed with larger data loads. This approach makes troubleshooting much easier and helps avoid unnecessary issues during migration.
I hope this blog gives you a clear understanding of the complete Customer Business Partner migration process in SAP S/4HANA 2025.
If you've worked on migration projects and have any useful tips or experiences, feel free to share them in the comments. I'd love to hear how you've approached customer migration in your projects.

Happy Learning!

Prashanth Gaddam
SAP S/4HANA SD Lead Consultant | 2× SAP Certified | Blogger | YouTuber
Sharing practical SAP knowledge through real-world examples, configuration tips, APIs, and SAP S/4HANA best practices.

entry.title: Don't Migrate for 2027. Build for 2028
entry.content:
Preparing the SAP ERP for Autonomous Business Processes

Having worked on multiple SAP transformation programs across industries, I have observed that many organizations still approach SAP S/4HANA primarily as a migration project rather than an opportunity to prepare for the next generation of SAP innovation.

Much of the SAP ecosystem continues to frame SAP S/4HANA transformation around the 2027 maintenance deadline. While that milestone remains important, organizations should use this transformation to build the foundation for the next generation of SAP Business AI rather than viewing it as the finish line.

SAP continues to invest heavily in Business AI, Joule, and intelligent business capabilities. Many of the innovations announced today and those still being developed will depend on foundations established during an SAP S/4HANA transformation. Clean-core architecture, trusted business data, standardized business processes, SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), and modern user experiences are becoming prerequisites for adopting future AI capabilities quickly and on a scale.

Rather than attempting to implement every new AI capability immediately, organizations should focus on building these foundational capabilities today. Doing so will enable them to adopt new SAP innovations as they become generally available, with significantly lower complexity, reduced technical debt, and faster business value.

Organizations that complete core activities such as process standardization, data governance, custom code remediation, Fiori adoption, and clean-core alignment will be better positioned to adopt autonomous capabilities as they mature.

The strategic question is therefore no longer just "How do we migrate before 2027?" It is "Are we building an ERP landscape that will be ready for the SAP innovations of 2028 and beyond?

SAP Sapphire Madrid 2026 reinforced SAP's strategic direction by expanding Business AI, Joule, and AI-powered business capabilities. While this momentum is encouraging, organizations should avoid prioritizing AI initiatives before establishing the architectural and operational foundations required to support them.

: The ECC maintenance runway — every option to the right of 2027 costs more and requires commitments. Verified against the SAP Support Portal maintenance strategy.

 

The data tells us the industry still has real work to do. According to the SAPinsider ERP Migration and Transformation Benchmark 2026 (296 respondents), a record 55% of organizations have deployed S/4HANA or S/4HANA Cloud — but only 34% have actually completed their transformation. And for the first time, S/4HANA Cloud adoption (26%) is nearly level with traditional on-premises S/4HANA (29%).

Where the SAP installed base stands in 2026: the 21-point gap between deployed (55%) and done (34%) is the real story. Source: SAPinsider Benchmark 2026, n = 296.

 Cloud as the Foundation for Autonomous Business Processes:

The objective of cloud transformation should extend beyond infrastructure modernization. It should prepare the ERP landscape for autonomous business processes. Building a clean core, standardizing business processes, improving data quality, and adopting a cloud operating model establish the foundation on which SAP Business AI, Joule, and future AI agents can deliver measurable business value. Without these foundations, AI initiatives risk becoming isolated innovations rather than enterprise-wide capabilities. 

For the first time, SAP's AI roadmap (43%) outranks the 2027 deadline (39%) as the primary driver of ERP strategy. Source: SAPinsider Benchmark 2026.

 

RISE vs. GROW: Selecting the Right Cloud Path

RISE with SAP and GROW with SAP provide different paths to SAP S/4HANA Cloud, each designed for different business needs. RISE is suited to organizations requiring greater flexibility and existing process continuity, while GROW is designed for organizations adopting standardized SAP Best Practices with continuous innovation.

The choice should be driven by business objectives, process standardization, regulatory requirements, and the desired operating model—not deployment preference alone.

Regardless of the chosen path, organizations should focus on building a clean core, trusted business data, standardized business processes, and SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) extensions. These foundations will enable organizations to adopt future SAP Business AI and Joule capabilities as they become available.

The Migration Paths, In Practice

No migration approach is inherently superior. The right choice is the one that best supports the organization's long-term business architecture and future AI strategy.

Approach

Best suited for

Brownfield (System Conversion)

Fastest route to SAP S/4HANA while preserving existing processes

Downtime-Optimized Conversion (DOC/NZDT)

Brownfield projects with strict downtime requirements

Selective Data Transition (Bluefield)

Organizations requiring selective transformation, carve-outs, mergers, or landscape consolidation

Greenfield (New Implementation)

Organizations redesigning business processes around SAP Best Practices

Re-platforming

Infrastructure modernization before or during ERP transformation

 

Lessons from Enterprise SAP Transformations

 Successful SAP S/4HANA transformation requires more than technical migration. Organizations should use the transformation to establish the foundation for future autonomous business processes.

  • Modernize the platform: For non-HANA landscapes, consider a phased transition through SAP Suite on HANA to reduce migration risk.
  • Validate the ecosystem: Assess third-party integrations, add-ons, interfaces, and custom developments early to ensure SAP S/4HANA compatibility.
  • Modernize custom code: Use SAP Custom Code Migration tools to reduce technical debt, retire obsolete developments, and align with clean-core principles.
  • Standardized business processes: Adopt SAP Best Practices wherever possible and minimize unnecessary customizations to simplify future innovation.
  • Drive SAP Fiori adoption: Fiori adoption requires users’ adoption, business process alignment, role redesign, change management, and stakeholder engagement, not just end-user training.
  • Build trusted business data: Archive obsolete data, improve master data quality, and establish governance to support analytics, AI, and automation.
  • Adopt an extension strategy: Build new capabilities on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) using side-by-side extensions rather than modifying the digital core.
  • Establish continuous innovation governance : Prepare for regular SAP releases with structured regression testing, release management, and operational readiness.
  • Deliver incrementally : Define an MVP based on SAP Best Practices, then expand capabilities through phased releases to accelerate value realization.

Preparing for the Next Generation of SAP Business AI

 SAP's recent innovations indicate that ERP transformation is moving beyond cloud migration toward AI-enabled business operations. Organizations planning SAP S/4HANA programs in 2026 should consider the following priorities:

Clean Core is becoming a strategic requirement: A clean-core architecture simplifies upgrades, enables continuous innovation, and provides the foundation for future SAP Business AI capabilities.

AI is changing application lifecycle management: AI-assisted testing, impact analysis, and automation through SAP Cloud ALM and partner solutions are reducing the effort required for upgrades and regression testing.

Industry Cloud accelerates business transformation: Industry-specific solutions enable organizations to adopt proven business capabilities while reducing implementation complexity.

Two-tier ERP is gaining momentum: Enterprises are increasingly adopting SAP S/4HANA at headquarters while supporting subsidiaries with standardized cloud ERP, creating a scalable operating model for global organizations.

Business value begins after go-live: The first months following implementation should focus on embedded analytics, SAP Business AI adoption, Joule enablement, and continuous business process optimization.

Skills remain a critical success factor: Successful transformation increasingly depends on expertise in cloud architecture, clean-core principles, SAP BTP, Business AI, and organizational change management.

Closing Thought

SAP S/4HANA should no longer be viewed simply as a response to the 2027 maintenance deadline. It is an opportunity to modernize business processes, simplify the digital core, improve data quality, and establish a cloud-ready operating model that supports continuous innovation.

Organizations that achieve the greatest long-term value will be those that use today's transformation programs to prepare their ERP landscape for autonomous business processes. By investing in a clean-core architecture, trusted business data, standardized processes, SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), and modern user experiences, they will be better positioned to adopt SAP Business AI, Joule, and future intelligent capabilities with greater agility and lower complexity.

I personally believe that organisations should not just proceed with S/4 HANA directly rather only focus on to build the baseline or foundation for new AI capabilities to be out in 2027 or 2028. There has to be shift on focus of budget keeping the focus on saving now to invest in future capabilities or upcoming technologies to be unleashed.

We have - Justice Delayed is justice denied which is true for SAP AI as well with the AI version as Opportunity delayed in opportunity denied. If the foundation is not ready then it will definitely lead to costs and lag of denied value creation in AI.

entry.content:
SAP Transition Workbench: Your Single Entry Point to a Smarter RISE Journey

Introduction

As organizations accelerate their move to SAP S/4HANA and cloud environments, the complexity of technical system transitions has become a critical challenge. Managing multiple tools, dependencies, and migration steps manually often introduces risk, delays, and operational inconsistency.

The RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench (STW) was designed to address exactly this challenge by providing a unified, automated, and guided approach to technical system migrations into the RISE with SAP Private Cloud Environment.

Instead of juggling multiple migration tools and processes, organizations can leverage a single orchestration platform that simplifies and standardizes their entire migration journey.

 

What Is SAP Transition Workbench?

The RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench (STW) serves as the single entry point for your RISE with SAP journey.

Rather than replacing established SAP migration tools, STW acts as an intelligent orchestration and automation layer that combines SAP Software Logistics tools into one guided workflow:

  • Software Update Manager (SUM)
  • Database Migration Option (DMO)
  • Software Provisioning Manager (SWPM)
  • Supporting SAP migration utilities

The result is a structured and standardized migration experience with automated checks, guided execution, and reduced operational risk.

Key Advantage

✅ One Entry Point
✅ One Guided Workflow
✅ One Standardized Migration Experience

The workbench is included within the RISE with SAP landscape at no additional cost and is pre-installed on the designated migration server.

Supported Migration Approaches (Cockpits)

Each migration scenario is delivered through a dedicated Cockpit, representing a predefined and SAP-supported migration path.

Supported Cockpits

Migration Approach

Description

SAP HANA Tenant Copy

High-speed migration using tenant copy technology

SAP HANA Backup & Recovery

Migration through backup and restore procedures

Homogeneous Update & Copy

Move SAP workloads to SAP Cloud infrastructure

SUM 2.0 DMO with System Move

Technical migration and database move in a single process

SUM 2.0 DMOVE2S4

System conversion to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition

 

Key Features & Benefits

Single Guided Entry Point

Benefits:

entry.title: SAP Cloud ERP (S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition) 2608亮点前瞻：跨技术话题（Cross Technology Topic）
entry.content:
时间过得很快，又到了版本升级的时刻。让我们来看看在2608版本中，跨技术话题领域有哪些值得关注的新功能。

 

1、数据迁移

1.1. “浏览迁移对象”App的增强

本次版本中，Explore Migration Objects（浏览迁移对象） 迎来了多项增强，进一步提升了迁移规划的透明度和效率，帮助项目团队更快识别可用迁移对象及其依赖关系。

1.1.1. 新增 Migration Object Availability（迁移对象可用性）状态

在 Migration Objects 视图中，新增 可用性 列，用于显示迁移对象当前是否可在系统中使用。系统会根据已激活的 Scope Item、Business Function 或 Feature Toggle 自动判断对象状态。

支持以下状态：

  • Yes：迁移对象已可用
  • No：迁移对象当前不可用
  • Conditional Yes：满足特定条件后可用，例如需要启用相关功能开关或业务功能

 

1.1.2. 新增 Scope Item 状态显示

应用现已支持显示 Scope Item 的激活状态，帮助实施团队快速确认对应业务场景是否已启用。

这意味着在规划数据迁移时，可以直接判断：

  • 哪些业务场景已经激活
  • 哪些迁移对象因 Scope Item 未激活而不可见
  • 是否需要提前完成业务范围（Scope）配置

1.1.3. 增强依赖关系图（Dependency Graph）

Dependency Graph 得到进一步优化，使迁移对象之间的前置依赖关系更加直观。

增强后可实现：

  • 更清晰地识别必需（Mandatory）和可选（Optional）的前置迁移对象
  • 支持按可用对象查看依赖关系
  • 支持分组（Group）/取消分组（Ungroup）显示

 

1.2. 2608版本中迁移对象的变化

同样，这个版本中也有新增、改变和删除的迁移对象，具体清单可见：

Change Overview for Release 2608 | SAP Help Portal

 

2、用户体验（UX）

2.1. 搜索框的变化

在2608版本中，对于最常用的右上角的搜索框进行了界面上的优化，重点提升搜索体验和结果浏览效率。主要变化包括：

  • 增加了一个清除按钮 X，可以快速地删除输入的内容。
  • 右边的放大镜图标，在搜索框输入内容的时候会变成蓝色，示意当前正在操作搜索框。
  • 搜索建议弹出窗口直接在搜索字段下方打开，并匹配其宽度，从而获得更清晰、更专注的搜索体验。

变化之前：

2608之前的搜索框

 

变化之后：

2608版本的搜索框

 

2.2. 单个重置快速启动板设置

在2608版本之前，如果我们进入“管理快速启动板设置”，想要把设置重置成默认值，我们只能选择重置全部，而不能单个重置。

2608版本之前重置快速启动板设置

 从2608版本开始，除了可以全部重置外，我们可以对单个设置进行重置，这样大大增加了灵活性。

2608版本的快速启动板设置重置

 

3、集成/API

3.1. 消息监控的业务目录弃用（需替换为新的业务目录）

对于集成来说，消息监控是最为常用的应用。从这个版本开始，相关的业务目录SAP_CA_BC_IC_LND_COM_ERR2_PC被标记为已弃用，代替为新的业务目录SAP_CA_BC_COM_CONF_PC。

 在应用“在升级后管理业务角色更改”中，页签“不赞成使用的业务目录”下，我们可以快速在相关的业务角色中替换业务目录：

 

3.2. 资产主数据通信场景（SAP_COM_0563）被替换

在 2608 版本中，SAP 正式弃用通信场景 SAP_COM_0563（Finance - Fixed Asset Integration）。除了固定资产主数据接口迁移至 SAP_COM_0A93 外，资产购置、报废和重估等业务接口迁移至 SAP_COM_0A95，基于工作量法（UoP）的使用对象接口迁移至 SAP_COM_0A96。SAP 建议客户逐步从原有 SOAP 服务切换到新的 OData V4 API 和通信场景。
不仅 Asset Master Data 的 SOAP API 被弃用，整个 SAP_COM_0563 通信场景也被弃用。 其中除了主数据接口迁移到 SAP_COM_0A93 外，其它固定资产业务接口也被拆分到了新的通信场景。

SAP_COM_0563 中的接口后继通信场景
Fixed Asset - Master Data (API_FIXEDASSET_G4BA)SAP_COM_0A93 
Fixed Asset : Usage Object for UoP Depreciation (API_FIXEDASSETUSAGEOBJECT_G4BA)SAP_COM_0A96 
Fixed Asset - Post Asset Acquisition (API_FIXEDASSETACQUISITION_G4BA)SAP_COM_0A95 
Fixed Asset - Post Asset Retirement (API_FIXEDASSETRETIREMENT_G4BA)SAP_COM_0A95 
Fixed Asset - Post Asset Revaluation (API_FIXEDASSETREVALUATION_G4BA)SAP_COM_0A95 

Fixed Asset - Create Main Asset (Asynchronous) (FAA_FIXED_ASSET_CREATE_MAIN_WEBI)
Fixed Asset - Create Main Asset (Asynchronous) Confirmation (CO_FAA_MD_ESR_CREATE_MAIN_CONF_SPRX)
Fixed Asset - Create Sub Asset (Asynchronous) (FAA_FIXED_ASSET_CREATE_SUB_WEBI)
Fixed Asset - Create Sub Asset (Asynchronous) Confirmation (CO_FAA_MD_ESR_CREATE_SUB_CONF_SPRX)
Fixed Asset - Change (Asynchronous) (FAA_FIXED_ASSET_CHANGE_WEBI)
Fixed Asset - Change (Asynchronous) Confirmation (CO_FAA_MD_ESR_CHANGE_CONF_SPRX)

OData V4 API_FIXEDASSET_G4BA（SAP_COM_0A93） 

 

以上是关于2608版本中跨技术话题的一些亮点更新介绍，如有任何问题，请留言。感谢阅读！

entry.title: Your One-Stop Shop for everything around Data Migration via SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit
entry.content:
If you are working with the SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit, whether you are just starting your migration journey or are knee-deep in a project, there is one page you must know:

The Landing Page for Data Migration on SAP Help Portal

Figure 1: Data Migration Landing

 

💡This blog describes the renovated landing pages for Public Cloud and SAP S/4HANA 2023FPS1+. The landing pages for all SAP S/4HANA releases below 2023FPS1 look different. Their look and feel is described in the blog Help for Starting Your Data Migration Journey to SAP S/4HANA Cloud by Anand Kapadia.

You can access the landing pages via the SAP Help Portal, Here you select your SAP S/4HANA Product that is either SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition or SAP S/4HANA.   
SAP provides two different flavors of that data migration landing page, dependent on your SAP S/4HANA product. Select solution SAP Business Suite → Enterprise resource planning. On the product page you scroll down to section Implement → Data Migration

❗The Data Migration landing page for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition is the same as for SAP S/4HANA. 

But to make your life easier to access the landing page for your specific product, you got two short aliases provided: 

  • https://help.sap.com/S4_OP_DM  (SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition)
  • https://help.sap.com/S4_CE_DM  (SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition)

The Data Migration landing pages of the SAP Help Portal contains more useful content than most people realize. Let's walk through what you will find:

Product Assistance — The Application Help

On left hand side, on the Table of Contents, you find the step-by-step documentation for everything the Migration Cockpit and all its complementing apps.

Figure 2: Application Help

 In general, you will find the following content there:

  • App documentation for the Explore Migration Objects Fiori app
  • App documentation for the Migrate Your Data – Migration Cockpit Fiori app
    • The two migration approaches: Migrate Using Staging Tables (works with any legacy system) and Migrate Data Directly from SAP System (SAP ECC to SAP S/4HANA...)
    • The migration process end-to-end: creating a project → selecting migration objects → mapping tasks → simulation → migrate
    • App documentation for the Data Migration Status Fiori app
    • App documentation for the Analyze Your Selection Process Fiori app
    • Information about Situation Handling for Data Migration

Getting Started - The Right Entry Point for First-Timers

If you are setting up the Migration Cockpit for the first time, the Getting Started section gives you a guided entry point covering:

Figure 3: Getting Started
  • The current presentation for the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit of the chosen product and release
  • Introduction videos for both migration approaches, the Migrate Using Staging Tables and Migrate Data Directly from SAP System(s)
  • Interactive Demos on several data migration apps and solutions

Learning - Train your Brain

The Learning section provides you with lots of learning and training materials to foster your knowledge:

 Figure 4: Learning

  • SAP Learning Course presents you the last course of the migration cockpit, that is for free
  • The document Cookbook for a SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit gives you practical guidance using the migration cockpit for common migration scenarios in its various flavors (SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition / SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition)
  • On Training Material page, you got presented training materials for the following topics:
    • Overview on the migration cockpit
    • Migrate Data Using Staging Tables
    • Migrate Data Directly from SAP System (Direct Transfer)
    • Migration Object Modeler - Files/Staging Tables
    • Migration Object Modeler - Direct Transfer
  • The Video Library for Data Migration for several apps and tools including cockpit, modeler, status app and others
  • You can also access the SAP Learning Hub directly
  • Links to the SAP Community topic page for the Migration Cockpit, which includes blog posts, Q&As, and the FAQ

 

Migration Objects

Available Migration Objects - The Searchable Catalogue

Reachable directly via the shortcut help.sap.com/S4_OP_MO (SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition) or  help.sap.com/S4_CE_MO  (SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition), this section is one of the most used resources for any migration project. It gives you a searchable table of all migration objects available in the current release, including: 

Figure 5: Available Migration Object List
  • Migration object name and corresponding business object type
  • Supported migration approach (Staging / Direct Transfer)
  • Custom field support (yes/no)
  • Component assignment (useful, in order to create support tickets)
  • Predecessor Object(s)
  • Supported by  Analyze Your Selection Process Fiori app (yes/no)

There are even more table fields in the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition:

  • Business Catalog name, needed to create own business roles to migrate this migration object
  • Sample Data applicable for the object (yes/no)
  • Scope item IDthat needs to be activated to make the object visible in migration cockpit (including link to SAP Signavio Process Navigator)

 

Figure 6: Available Migration Object List

This table is your answer to "Can I migrate this with the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit?" before you even open the system.

Object-Related Information - Templates, Samples & Supplements

This section is often overlooked but packed with practical content:

Figure 7: Object Related Information
  • Data Migration Template Samples: Pre-filled example XML/CSV files to help you understand the expected format before building your own
  • Release Comparison of Migration Object Templates: Shows you what changed between releases.  It explains the differences between the templates of different releases by directly comparing them.
    • Which migration objects are new in the current release
    • Which migration objects are deprecated or removed
    • What has changed in existing objects' templates (added/removed fields, structural changes, name changes, position changes...)
  • Support of Custom Fields: Provides information about how and for which migration objects you can add custom fields (Key-User Extensibility)
    • ❗The migration cockpit only supports custom fields for APIs that uses extensibility model Key-User Extensibility are registered for Data Migration within the extensibility model definition.  Classical Extensibility known from SAP ECC, especially the BAPI EXTENSION structure model,  is NOT supported. 
  • Migration of Financial Data: The documentation Migration of Financial Accounting Master Data and Transactional Data is the reference guide you must know to migration financial data

🔔Tip: Checking this section after each release should be standard practice for any migration project team.

Project Organization

This section contains links to help with organizing your projects such as:

Figure 8: Project Organization
  • The link to the SAP Activate Roadmap
  • The SAP Signavio Process Navigator solution process for the Migrate Using Staging Tables approach (2Q2) on SAP for Me
  • SAP Signavio Process Navigator solution process for the Migrate Data Directly from SAP System approach (BH3) on SAP for Me (only available for Public Cloud)

The following information is only available on the landing page for SAP S/4HANA:

  • Information on the Note Analyzer transaction CNV_NA_MC to regularly check if all correction notes for the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit are implemented
  • License Note - Staging Tables, useful information about SAP HANA license to check if you can run staging tables on a remote database connection
❗You need an active user on SAP for Me to access the SAP Signavio Process Navigator

Last Quick Tip: The Three Aliases You Must Know

No searching, no clicking through product hierarchies, just type the alias and you are there.

Here are the three most important shortcuts for SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition:

AliasWhat you get
help.sap.com/S4_OP_DMData Migration landing page
help.sap.com/S4_OP_MOAvailable Migration Objects overview
help.sap.com/S4_OP_DM_STATUSData Migration Status app page

And here the three most important shortcuts for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

AliasWhat you get
help.sap.com/S4_CE_DMData Migration landing page
help.sap.com/S4_CE_MOAvailable Migration Objects overview
help.sap.com/S4_CE_DM_STATUSData Migration Status app page

entry.title: From Any Source to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Complete SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit Guide
entry.content:
In almost every S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition project data migration is the longest and often underestimated workstream, that causes the most stress closest to go-live. The questions are always the same: which approach do we use, what can be migrated?

This blog tries to answer all of this in one place by using SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit, accessible via the SAP Fiori Migrate Your Data app as the thread. Whether you're coming from - a non-SAP legacy system, SAP ERP, or SAP Business ByDesign or SAP Business One - there is a defined path and knowing it upfront saves a lot of effort later.

 

Which Approach Is Right for You? Quick Decision Guide

Before diving into the details, here's the short version:

Your Current SystemMigration ApproachKey Consideration
Non-SAP / custom SAP ERPStaging TablesBroadest migration object coverage; data prep effort is highest
SAP ERPDirect TransferCoverage of available migration objects is lower, streamlined
SAP Business ByDesignStaging TablesBuilt-in extraction tool available for data preparation and transformation for most objects
SAP Business OneStaging TablesQueries for Data extraction and tools for data transformation provided for key objects on Business Accelerator Hub

If your source system is in that table, read the relevant section below. If you're evaluating multiple options, read all four.

 

The Shared Starting Point: Always a New Implementation

Before discussing the differences, the most important, common characteristic should be highlighted: the migration to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition is always a new implementation (greenfield), independent of source system.

There is no system conversion (brownfield), and no selective data transition in the traditional SAP ERP sense if the target is the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Configuration, business processes, and integrations must be (re)built using SAP Best Practices. Only the business data are transferred.

 

Migration from non-SAP /Custom SAP ERP to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Using the Migrate Data Using Staging Tables Approach (aka Staging Tables)

How it works

The SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit creates temporary database tables - staging tables - for each migration object in your migration project. You populate these by uploading data via SAP-provided XML or CSV templates, or by feeding data in directly through ETL tools. Once the data is in staging tables, the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit validates it, lets you apply value mappings, and then transfers it into your S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.

For more information about the Migrate Data Using Staging Tables: see SAP Help Portal.

What's available

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition ships with 240 migration objects (CE 2608) for the staging tables approach, covering customers, suppliers, products, AR/AP open items, G/L account balances, and much more.

For available migration objects see: https://help.sap.com/S4_CE_MO - select the migration approach Staging Table.

Ideal Use cases

  • Migrating from non-SAP legacy systems
  • SAP ERP: Where data needs significant cleansing and transformation before load, the available migration object scope of the direct transfer approach is not sufficient, or the SAP system is below SAP ECC 6.0
  • Projects where an ETL tool or partner tooling is used to feed the staging tables

Who is this for?

This approach suits the broadest customer segment: any company moving to S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition regardless of their source system. It is the default choice for net-new cloud customers, companies replacing a non-SAP system, and organizations that need full control over data transformation before it enters the target system.

 

Migration from SAP ERP to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Using the Migrate Data Directly from SAP System Approach (aka Direct Transfer)

How it works

Rather than using files, the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit establishes a direct connection to your existing SAP ERP system. Data is extracted from the source and transferred directly into you S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. This requires that the SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud Edition is based on 3-system-landscape, your source system is an SAP ECC 6.0 and DMIS 2011 SP25+ add-on is installed, and the communication arrangement SAP_COM_0816 is created on the target side (see solution process: BH3 on SAP Signavio Process Navigator)

As of CE2602, SAP introduced optional Staging Tables as Intermediate Storage feature for direct transfer, giving you greater transparency and the ability to review and adjust data before it is transferred to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. This required, in addition, that the communication arrangement SAP_COM_0678 is created. (see solution process 2Q2 SAP Signavio Process Navigator). 

For more information about the Migrate Data Directly from SAP System see: SAP Help Portal.

💡Tip:

  • See blog from Mirella Vorsprach: Migration Cockpit in SAP Cloud ERP 2602
  • See blog from Philipp Kreutzheide: SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit – Migrate Data Directly from SAP System – Using Staging Tables

What's available

The direct transfer approach currently covers 24 migration objects (CE2608), fewer than the staging tables approach.

For available Migration Objects: https://help.sap.com/S4_CE_MO - select the migration approach Direct Transfer.

Ideal Use Cases

  • Companies running SAP ECC 6.0 moving to S/4HANA Public Cloud Edition
  • Projects where the required migration objects fall within the supported 24-migration object scope
  • Scenarios where the source data is already well-structured and largely clean
  • Migrations were minimizing manual file handling and reducing transformation effort is a priority

Who is this for?

This approach targets SAP ERP customers making the move to the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. It is common in the mid-market and in subsidiaries of larger SAP customers that run SAP ERP and are now standardizing on SAP Cloud Public Edition.

 

Migration from SAP Business ByDesign to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Using the Migrate Data Using the Staging Tables Approach 

Context

SAP delisted SAP Business ByDesign from its price list for new customers on 20 April 2026. Existing customers remain fully supported, there is no announced end date, but SAP's strategic direction is clear: The successor platform for the mid-market is SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

How it works

Instead, it relies on a file-based / template-driven approach, which maps to the staging tables approach in the S/4HANA migration cockpit. Data is first exported from SAP Business ByDesign using the built-in self-service extraction tool, then mapped and transformed (using the tools provided on Business Accelerator Hub) to match the S/4HANA migration object structure and finally loaded into the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit's staging tables via template upload. From there, the standard migration process runs.

👉 SAP Business ByDesign does not use the direct transfer approach.

💡Tip:

  • SAP provides a dedicated learning path for this scenario: Migrating Data from SAP Business ByDesign to SAP S/4HANA Cloud.
  • See blog from Babu Lal Limba: Data Extraction from SAP Business ByDesign for Migration to Cloud ERP

What's available

The built-in SAP ByDesign extraction tool supports the most common migration objects: master data, transactional data, and accounting data. On the target side, the full set of ~240 migration objects (CE2608) of the staging tables approach in S/4HANA Public Cloud is available.

Ideal Use Cases

  • Companies that have outgrown SAP Business ByDesign functionally and need a more scalable platform
  • Migration of master data (business partners, products,…) and open items from SAP Business ByDesign
  • Projects leveraging the built-in extraction tool to pull data cleanly and structurally from SAP Business ByDesign
  • Strategic consolidations where multiple SAP Business ByDesign tenants are merged into a single S/4HANA instance

Who is this for?

SAP Business ByDesign customers are typically mid-sized companies (50–500 users) who originally chose the cloud-native SAP Business ByDesign for its simplicity and lower TCO. Migration to S/4HANA Public Cloud Edition is the next step for those who have grown beyond SAP Business ByDesign’s functional scope, or who want to align with SAP's long-term platform strategy proactively, ahead of any future support changes.

 

Migration from SAP Business One to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Using the Migrate Data Using the Staging Tables Approach

How it works

For SAP Business One customers migrating to S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the route is through staging tables approach: data is extracted from SAP Business One, using direct database queries, or partner tooling, mapped to SAP-provided XML migration templates and then loaded into the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit. Because SAP Business One's data model differs significantly from S/4HANA Public Cloud Edition's, the transformation and mapping phase requires particular care. SAP has provided tools to extract and transform the data, for some of the key objects in SAP Business One, into SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition format for upload.

👉 SAP Business One is also not a supported source system for the direct transfer approach.

What's available

On the target side, the full set of 240 migration objects (CE2608) of the staging tables approach in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition is available. There is no native extraction interface from SAP Business One into the SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit - data preparation is entirely the responsibility of the customer or implementation partner.

Ideal Use Cases

  • Migration of master data and transactional data from SAP Business One into S/4HANA Cloud Public Editon
  • Projects where partner tooling or custom ETL tools bridge the gap between the SAP Business One data model and S/4HANA structure
  • Consolidations where SAP Business One is replaced by S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition as the central platform

Who is this for?

SAP Business One customers are typically small to mid-sized businesses (up to ~50 users) that have either outgrown the platform or are seeking a more capable foundation for further growth. Migration requires investment in data preparation, but the staging approach gives teams full control over data quality before anything goes live.

 

Key Principles: Regardless of Approach

A few things hold true across all four migration scenarios:

  • The migration cockpit is an initial load tool. It inserts data; it does not update or sync. Migrated records cannot be re-migrated or deleted from the target
  • Historical data (e.g. past invoices, completed orders) cannot be migrated
  • Valid ≠ correct. The migration cockpit will accept values that are technically valid but business-incorrect (e.g. wrong groupings). Value mapping decisions require domain expertise, not just technical mapping
  • Test before you migrate. Run migration tests in a dedicated test system before the productive load.
  • Data quality is a business task, not an IT task. The earlier business stakeholders are involved in data cleansing and sign-off, the smoother the go-live

 

Conclusion

The SAP Fiori Migrate Your Data app (SAP S/4HANA migration cockpit) covers all four scenarios described above. When you understand which path applies to your source system, the project becomes significantly more predictable. The biggest lever in every migration is not the approach itself; it's how early you start assessing data quality and involving the right people.

If you're currently planning a migration project, the first practical step is a data assessment: which objects need to move, how clean the source data is, and which of the available migration objects you need. Everything else follows from there.

💡Tip: For that data assessment step, the SAP Fiori Explore Migration Objects app is exactly the right starting point. It gives you a structured view of all migration objects available for the staging table approach and their dependencies. It also shows which migration objects are assigned to a given scope item.
